newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean economy nearly bottomed out-analysts.
newsitem.headline: South Korean economy nearly bottomed out-analysts.

text.p: A surge in industrial output in April and a 10-year low in consumer inflation in May shows that the beleagured South Korean economy has nearly touched bottom, economists said on Friday.
The nation's industrial production rose 10.7 percent year-on-year in April, up from an 8.4 percent rise a year earlier, National Statistical Office (NSO) figures showed.
The Ministry of Finance and Economy also reported 3.8 percent year-on-year inflation in May, as measured by the consumer price index (CPI), the lowest since May 1987 when it rose 2.6 percent.

"April industrial output figures raise hopes of an imminent economic recovery. Despite the high growth in inventories, the prospects of recovery are bright because of improving global demand," said Han Sang-choon, economist at Daewoo Research Institute.
Output in April inproved because of an increase in 64-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chip production and vehicle exports, the office said.
Production of semiconductors in April rose 55.4 percent on the year, while office accounting equipment such as personal computers increased 46.9 percent. Inventories in the month
rose 13.2 percent year-on-year, compared with an 18.5 percent rise a year ago, the NSO said.
"An economic recovery will take place gradually because of still high levels of inventories," said Kim Kwang-yul, economist at Dongwon Economic Research Institute.
The NSO figures showed the factory operating rate stood at 82.5 percent in April, against 82.7 percent a year ago.

Domestic machinery orders, a leading investment indicator, rose 17.6 percent year-on-year compared with 11.7 percent a year earlier, but imports of machinery dropped 18.8 percent, against a rise of 23.6 percent.
Economists said slowing inflation also brightened prospects for an economic recovery.

"The low level of consumer inflation shows a typical cyclical point where an economic bottom is being reached. If the current trend holds, the CPI will be limited to below four percent this year," said Kim Sung-shik, economist at LG Economic Research Institute.
"Given the high levels of inventories, the economic bottom will be reached in the third quarter of this year."

A ministry official said CPI in May slowed as prices for farm goods continued to stabilise due to favourable weather. Prices for agricultural, livestock and fisheries products rose 1.2 percent year-on-year in the month.
Beef prices, excluding imports, fell 14.4 percent, and potatoes dropped 34.9 percent, the ministry said.
Prices for industrial products rose a year-on-year four percent, led by a 25.5 percent rise in oil products.
But industrial product prices, excluding oil products, rose 1.1 percent year-on-year, the ministry said.
"The slowing economy and intensifying competition in distribution helped keep industrial prices in check," said Yoon Sung-ho, director of the ministry's price division.
The NSO also said the nation's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 2.7 percent in April from 1.9 percent a year earlier.
The NSO figures showed the economically active population rose to 21.82 million in April from 21.17 million a year ago and from 21.46 million in March.
